provenance.translation: Direct translation of the public Japanese guide. Existing source metadata remains with the original guide; proper names use the paired game localization dictionary.

lead.text: In form 1, win Clashes against “Golden Fruit” to reduce healing. At 1 HP, an event check leads to the next form. In form 2, break the Head to stop all Parts next turn, then use that opening to defeat the main body.

listLead.text: Win the Clashes that reduce healing and break parts to create openings. A break does not instantly stop every attack, so maintain the rest of that turn's pairings.

statNote.text: The final battle on Floor 3 of the Canto I dungeon. Form 1: Lv. 8, 316 main-body HP, 214 Body HP. Form 2: Lv. 8, 383 main-body HP, 50 Head HP, 201 Body HP. HP entries distinguish main-body and Part HP. Stats from Thread Luxcavation or enhanced versions do not apply.

skillNote.text: All 6 skills of the normal Canto I version. These differ from the higher-Power skills of enhanced versions. Form 1 uses enemy level − 2 for Offense and Defense Levels; form 2 uses enemy level + 2. Breaking the Head stops actions next turn, not on the turn it breaks.

priorities.0.text: Win Clashes against “Golden Fruit”. This deals 20 damage to the enemy and reduces Golden Sheen by 1, lowering its Turn Start healing.

priorities.1.text: Form 1 stops at 1 HP and triggers a check at Turn End. Both success and failure lead to form 2, so its survival is not a bug.

priorities.2.text: In form 2, break the Head with Blunt attacks to stop all Parts next turn. It still attacks on the turn the Head breaks, so maintain your Clashes.

troubleshooting.0.symptom.text: It keeps healing and the fight will not end

troubleshooting.0.advice.text: Form 1 heals 10 HP per Golden Sheen at Turn Start. It starts with 3, healing 30 HP. Win against “Golden Fruit” to reduce this value, and focus your attacks.

troubleshooting.1.symptom.text: Its HP will not drop below 1

troubleshooting.1.advice.text: In Canto I, reduce form 1 to 1 HP and proceed to the Turn End check. Other encounters may change forms on Body destruction alone; that condition does not apply here.

troubleshooting.2.symptom.text: Breaking the Head did not stop the attacks

troubleshooting.2.advice.text: Head destruction stops all Parts next turn. It still attacks on the turn the Head breaks, so Clash against the remaining skills.

troubleshooting.3.symptom.text: Debuffs disappeared after the form change

troubleshooting.3.advice.text: Form 2 is treated as a separate enemy, resetting debuffs applied to form 1. After the change, choose actions based on the new HP and attacks.

units.0.notes.0.text: Starts with 3 Golden Sheen. Can still be attacked after destruction and continues acting.

units.0.notes.1.text: In Canto I, reaching 1 main-body HP triggers a Turn End check and a transition to the next form.

units.1.notes.0.text: Can still be attacked after destruction. Attacks do not stop on the turn it breaks.

units.1.notes.1.text: All Parts stop acting for the next 1 turn. The Head regenerates 1 turn after destruction.

units.2.notes.0.text: Can still be attacked after destruction and continues acting. Its slot weight is 2.

units.2.notes.1.text: Destruction grants 2 Attack Power Down to all Parts from the next turn onward.

phases.0.title.text: Reduce healing and bring main-body HP down to 1

phases.0.steps.0.text: The battle starts with 3 Golden Sheen. At Turn Start, it heals Golden Sheen × 10 HP, so prioritize winning against “Golden Fruit”. Each win deals 20 damage and removes 1 Golden Sheen.

phases.0.steps.1.text: Blunt and Sloth are effective. Form 1 alternates between 2 “Sprout”, 1 “Golden Fruit”, and 1 “Solid Gold”, and 2 “Golden Fruit” plus 2 “Solid Gold”. Take necessary Clashes and use spare actions to damage the main body.

phases.0.steps.2.text: The Body remains targetable and active after destruction. In Canto I, the event occurs at the end of the turn when main-body HP reaches 1; do not apply Part-break conditions from other encounters.

phases.1.timing.text: Main-body HP at 1 / Turn End check

phases.1.title.text: Avoid failure's extra damage while changing forms

phases.1.steps.0.text: The check favors Sloth, and Gregor receives a +4 bonus. The required value is listed as 6 (9 in parentheses), so choose using the success prediction displayed in battle.

phases.1.steps.1.text: Both success and failure lead to the next form. Failure costs the selected Sinner 25 HP and grants 3 Damage Up to all Parts for 2 turns. Aim for success; if you fail, watch for increased damage immediately after the transition.

phases.1.steps.2.text: Form 2 is treated as a different enemy; debuffs from form 1 do not carry over. Switch to reducing its new 383 main-body HP.

phases.2.timing.text: Form 2 / turns with the Head intact

phases.2.title.text: Maintain Clashes on the turn you break the Head

phases.2.steps.0.text: The Head has 50 Part HP and is weak to Blunt. Match strong skills against “Deteriorating Flesh” and “Entangle”, preventing Bleed, Fragile, and main-body healing while damaging the Head.

phases.2.steps.1.text: Breaking the Head stops all Parts next turn. It does not cancel every attack immediately, so maintain the current turn's Clashes.

phases.2.steps.2.text: The Body's Nutrient Absorption also heals HP if its second Coin hits. Keep enough actions for necessary Clashes rather than spending everything on the Head.

phases.3.title.text: Focus damage on the main body while all Parts are inactive

phases.3.steps.0.text: All Parts stop for 1 turn after Head destruction. Focus strong attacks to finish the main body. The Head regenerates, so prepare for attacks to resume if the boss survives.

phases.3.steps.1.text: The Head has ×2 Blunt resistance; the Body has ×2 Slash and ×1.5 Blunt. Choose targets based on your skills' physical types. Breaking the Body also grants 2 Attack Power Down to all Parts from next turn onward, helping recovery.

phases.3.steps.2.text: Form 2 has no normal Stagger Thresholds. Use the special shutdown from Head destruction rather than HP-based Stagger.

skills.0.response.text: Form 1's normal attack. Take necessary Clashes while reserving skills that can beat “Golden Fruit”.

skills.1.response.text: Winning the Clash deals 20 damage to the enemy and removes 1 Golden Sheen. This skill is key to reducing its healing, so match it with a strong skill.

skills.2.response.text: Form 1's Guard skill. Prioritize Clashes against attacks, especially winning against “Golden Fruit”, then use spare actions on the main body.

skills.3.effects.0.text: Ⅱ[On Hit] Heal 3 HP for the main body.

skills.3.response.text: Coin 2 heals 3 main-body HP on hit. Take necessary Clashes against Body attacks as well as Head attacks.

skills.4.effects.0.text: Ⅰ[On Hit] Increase Bleed Count by 3 next turn.

skills.4.response.text: On Hit, adds 3 Bleed Count and inflicts 2 Fragile next turn. Use strong skills against the Head to prevent these effects while reducing its 50 HP. Head destruction stops actions from next turn onward.

skills.5.effects.0.text: Ⅱ[On Hit] Heal 10 HP for the main body.

skills.5.response.text: Coin 2 heals 10 main-body HP on hit and inflicts 5 Bleed next turn. Remaining attacks still happen on the turn the Head breaks, so do not abandon Clashes in reliance on destruction alone.

passives.0.effect.text: Heal HP proportional to Golden Sheen. Its effect heals stacks × 10 HP at Turn Start.

passives.0.response.text: Win against “Golden Fruit” to reduce the stacks. Leaving it at its initial 3 stacks allows 30 HP healing each turn.

passives.1.effect.text: All Parts stop acting for the next 1 turn. The destroyed Head regenerates after 1 turn.

passives.1.response.text: Attacks remain on the turn it breaks. Focus on the main body during the safe opening next turn.

passives.2.effect.text: All Parts gain 2 Attack Power Down from the next turn onward.

passives.2.response.text: Besides stopping actions by breaking the Head, you can weaken later attacks by breaking the Body.

mechanics.0.effect.text: Starts at 3. At Turn Start, heal stacks × 10 HP. Losing a Clash with “Golden Fruit” reduces stacks by 1.

mechanics.0.response.text: Winning the Clash as a Sinner reduces its healing. Prioritize “Golden Fruit” rather than only making unopposed attacks against Guard.

mechanics.1.effect.text: Form 1 cannot reach 0 HP. At the end of the turn when it reaches 1 HP, a check occurs. Both success and failure lead to form 2. Debuffs from form 1 are reset.

mechanics.1.response.text: Reduce main-body HP to 1 and proceed to the check. Passing it does not end the battle itself.

mechanics.2.effect.text: Breaking the Head stops all Parts for the following 1 turn. Actions continue on the turn it breaks, and the Head regenerates after 1 turn.

mechanics.2.response.text: Clash against current attacks and concentrate damage next turn. This effect is separate from normal Stagger.

warnings.0.text: Reaching 1 HP in form 1 triggers phase progression. It is not a normal kill awaiting resolution.

warnings.1.text: Failing the transition check costs 25 HP and grants the enemy 3 Damage Up for 2 turns. Even success continues into form 2.

warnings.2.text: All Parts still act on the turn the Head breaks. Next turn's shutdown is not an immediate cancellation.

warnings.3.text: Form 2 has no normal Stagger Thresholds. Use the shutdown after Head destruction and reduced Power after Body destruction.

preparation.0.text: Deploy 5 Sinners. Prepare your core team's levels, HP, and SP using the dungeon's recommended Lv. 7 and the enemy's Lv. 8 as guides.

preparation.1.text: Bring Blunt attacks effective against your intended Parts in both forms. Wrath and Sloth are also effective. Focusing Slash on form 1 runs into its ×0.5 resistance.

preparation.2.text: The transition check favors Sloth. Check Gregor's bonus and choose a Sinner who can withstand losing 25 HP on failure.

roles.0.reason.text: Reduce Golden Sheen to suppress healing in form 1.

roles.1.reason.text: Reduce form 2's 50 Head HP to stop all Parts next turn.

roles.2.reason.text: Avoid the damage bonus immediately after the transition. Gregor's +4 bonus can help.
